turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning, I'm Jess, one of the nurses. I'll just do your observations before the doctor comes through. Pop your arm out for me.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Good morning. Yes, of course. Thank you.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Blood pressure is one eighteen over seventy-two, pulse is eighty-eight, and your temperature is thirty-six point six. All very settled.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): That is a relief to hear.
[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): I've also checked a urine pregnancy test, and it's positive. Your partner's still out in the waiting room. Did you want him to stay there for now?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, please. I would prefer to speak with the doctor first, if that is all right.
[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hello, I'm Dr Shah. Come and sit down. What's been going on?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you, doctor. I believe I am pregnant, and for the last few days I have had some spotting, and cramps as well. I am quite worried.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'm glad you came in. Tell me about the spotting in your own words.

[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): It began, um, about a week ago. Well, actually, no, forgive me, it has been three days. It is light, brown at first, and this morning there was a little pink on the paper.
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any flooding, or clots, or anything that looked like tissue?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing like that. It has not soaked a pad.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): And the cramps?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): They started two days ago. Low down, they come and go. I would call them mild, though they woke me once last night.
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): How far along do you think you are?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): I am not certain of my dates, doctor. The last period was around Diwali, or after. Perhaps eight weeks, or it may be ten. I cannot pin the day down.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): That's all right, we'll work with what we have. Any nausea, or breast tenderness?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Some nausea in the mornings, yes, mild. The breasts have been a little tender, but that is not new this week.
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): Have you felt feverish at all?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): No, I have not had a fever.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any pain at the tip of your shoulder, or pain when you pass urine?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): No shoulder pain, and passing urine is normal. No burning.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): How are you feeling in yourself, apart from the worry?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): I have been very anxious, doctor. I did not sleep much last night. I keep thinking something is wrong.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): That's completely understandable. Any pregnancies or operations before this?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): This is my first pregnancy. I had my appendix removed when I was sixteen. Nothing else.
[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): Are you taking any medicines, including anything from the chemist?

[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): I take folic acid, five hundred micrograms, one tablet each morning, by mouth. I started it when I suspected I was pregnant. This morning I also took two Panadol for the cramps, that is one thousand milligrams, just the once.
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any allergies to medicines or anything else?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): No, I have no allergies that I know of.
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke, or drink alcohol?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): I have never smoked. I did drink a glass of wine on weekends, but I stopped completely once I thought I might be pregnant. I live with my partner.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): There is one other thing from before. About a year ago my GP checked my thyroid, and they said it was borderline. I did not go back for the repeat blood test.
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): Thanks for telling me. We won't treat that as a diagnosis today, just something you've recalled.
[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): Before I examine you, you look like you've had a morning of it. Was the traffic awful getting here?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): It was dreadful, doctor. We were stuck on Parramatta Road for nearly forty minutes, and then we could not find a park.
[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yeah, that road is a car park after eight. Did you catch any of the cricket last night?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): My partner had it on. I am afraid I do not follow it closely. He was very pleased about the wicket, I think in the last over.
[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): Ha, a last-over wicket will do that. The weather didn't help either, did it. That storm came through just as I was leaving home.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, the rain was quite heavy. We had to run from the car with a newspaper over our heads. Rather undignified.
[SEG0041] person_3 (DOCTOR): I did the same with my jacket. Righto, back to you. Hop up on the bed and I'll have a gentle feel of your tummy. You can leave your pants on.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Of course. Thank you.
[SEG0043] person_3 (DOCTOR): Abdomen's soft. There's mild tenderness low down, a little more towards the middle. No guarding, and I'm not pressing hard.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): It is uncomfortable, but bearable.

[SEG0045] person_3 (DOCTOR): So, thinking out loud, spotting and cramps at this stage can be a few different things. It may be a threatened miscarriage, and I also can't exclude an ectopic pregnancy until we know where it is sitting. I am not going to conclude either one today. The scan has to tell us.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): I understand. I would rather know properly.

[SEG0047] person_3 (DOCTOR): My first thought is to send you home and book a pelvic ultrasound for Thursday, and your GP can chase the result. The urine test is already positive, so we know that much.
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): Thursday. Yes, if you think that is safe.

[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): Doctor, I am sorry, I should have said this earlier. Since last night the cramp has been more on the right side, not just in the middle. And when I got out of the car I felt light-headed for a minute. It passed when I sat down.
[SEG0050] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'm glad you said that. That changes my plan. I don't want to wait until Thursday. We'll do the ultrasound today, before you leave the clinic.
[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): Today would be better. Thank you.
[SEG0052] person_3 (DOCTOR): And I'll add blood tests today as well, a quantitative pregnancy hormone, the beta-hCG, and your blood group and antibodies. Not Thursday, today.
[SEG0053] person_1 (NURSE): I can take her across for the bloods after the scan is booked. Shall I bring her partner in now? He's been asking at the desk.
[SEG0054] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes, please, if she's happy.
[SEG0055] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, I would like him to come in. Thank you, nurse.
[SEG0056] person_1 (NURSE): I've shown him in. He's just by the chair. I'll get the request forms printed.
[SEG0057] person_3 (DOCTOR): Thanks for waiting outside. You can sit with her. We're arranging a scan and some bloods this morning, so you'll both be here a bit longer.
[SEG0058] person_2 (PATIENT): He was very worried, which is why he came. I am grateful you are doing the tests today.
[SEG0059] person_3 (DOCTOR): Keep taking the folic acid each morning. Don't take ibuprofen or Nurofen while this is unsettled. Paracetamol, like the Panadol you had, is fine if the cramps need it.
[SEG0060] person_2 (PATIENT): I will do that. No ibuprofen.
[SEG0061] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'll see you back this afternoon, once the scan and the bloods are through, so we can go over them together.

[SEG0062] person_3 (DOCTOR): And this part is important. If the bleeding soaks a pad within an hour, or the pain becomes severe, or you feel faint or develop shoulder pain, come straight back to emergency, don't wait for this afternoon.
[SEG0063] person_2 (PATIENT): I understand. If any of those happen, we will go to emergency immediately. Thank you for explaining it so clearly.
[SEG0064] person_3 (DOCTOR): You're welcome. Jess will walk you both over. We'll take this one step at a time.

spec.situation: Woman about 8-10 weeks pregnant with spotting and cramps; unsure of dates ('the last period was around Diwali, or after'); anxious; partner waits outside then joins. Scan and blood tests planned today, strict return advice.
features: doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.
doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.
test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.
tangent_small_talk: a long tangent or small talk (traffic, cricket, the weather, a grandchild) that holds NO clinical content; nothing from it is extracted.
